tickets.title: Improve DX for Installation and Usage Docs
tickets.body: Update README.md and docs/usage.md to streamline the 'how to install' and 'how to use' sections. Ensure the text flows well for new developers. Also, create docs/fumadocs-plan.md outlining a strategy to migrate all docs to Fumadocs.

tickets.title: Resolve adlc plugin via npm node_modules
tickets.body: Update `lib/bootstrap.mjs` to seamlessly install the `adlc-antigravity` plugin. Resolve `@adlc/antigravity-plugin` from `node_modules` using `require.resolve`. If it fails, fallback to the local sibling directory `../adlc/plugins/adlc-antigravity`. Add it to `dependencies` in `package.json`.

tickets.title: [P2] feat: append-only events.jsonl for RunStatus
tickets.body:
Implement atomic event logs for the dashboard.

1. Modify `RunStatus` constructor in `lib/status.mjs` to accept `(repo, runId)`. Update `lib/scheduler.mjs` to pass `runId`.
2. Add an `appendEvent(event)` internal function to `RunStatus`. Use a singleton write queue wrapping `await fs.promises.appendFile`. Stringify the event payload synchronously before appending it to the async queue, so rapid mutations to `pools` don't overwrite states. Add a `.catch()` block within the `this.writePromise` chain so that a single write failure doesn't halt the entire run.
3. Modify `status.ticket()` and `status.pools()` to immediately append an event after mutating state. `from` is the `phase` value before the update. `to` maps to `patch.phase`. `detail`, `model`, `strikes` map exactly to `patch`. The `pools` field should just be the raw `this.state.pools` map.
4. Rename `status.finish` to `status.report(summary)`. It continues to write the summary JSON to `.booster/report.json`, but it now also appends a `report` event.
5. Add `status.strike(ticketId, { model, error, strikes })`. It updates state (store `error` directly on the ticket, set `strikes` to the argument, initialize if missing) and flushes to `run.json`, then appends a `strike` event.
6. `.booster/logs/<runId>/events.jsonl` Schema: `{ ts, runId, type: 'phase'|'pool'|'strike'|'report', ticket?, from?, to?, detail?, pools?, model?, error?, done?, report? }`. `ts` is an ISO 8601 string.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replay test dynamically generates events and recreates `run.json` state (merge tickets with `Object.assign`, replace pools).

tickets.title: [P2] feat: normalize transcripts to JSONL
tickets.body:
Normalize per-ticket transcripts to JSONL and update consumers.

1. Normalize per-ticket transcripts to JSONL: one record per agy invocation `{ ts, model, strike, ms, ok, role, error, prompt, output, cwd }`. `role` is mandatory (e.g. 'builder' or 'prosecutor').
2. In `lib/agy.mjs` and `lib/prosecute.mjs`, both builder and prosecutor MUST append to `<ticketId>.jsonl` using `fs.promises.appendFile`.
3. `runAgy` should always write JSONL to `logFile` regardless of the file extension (remove the legacy write branch). `runId` is NOT passed to `runAgy` or `prosecute()`; they receive the exact `logFile` path.
4. In `lib/scheduler.mjs`, change the prosecutor log path passed to `prosecute()` from `<ticketId>.prosecution.jsonl` to `<ticketId>.jsonl`.
5. In `lib/scheduler.mjs` (`checkFlailDetector`), deserialize the JSONL transcript back to raw legacy text using the `role` field to map back correctly. Write it to a temporary file using `crypto.randomUUID()` in `os.tmpdir()` for a unique filename, pass that temp file path to `adlc flail-detector`, and then delete it.
6. Update `docs/usage.md` with semantic descriptions for all fields across `events.jsonl` and `<ticketId>.jsonl`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Transcripts parse as JSONL.
- `test/prosecute.test.mjs` expects JSONL.
- `fake-adlc` keeps working.

tickets.title: [P2] refactor: rebuild TUI rendering on @earendil-works/pi-tui (supersedes T3)
tickets.body:
Rebuild the rendering layer of `lib/tui.mjs` on `@earendil-works/pi-tui`.

This is a RENDERING-LAYER change, not a redesign. What a frame CONTAINS must not change; only how frames reach the terminal changes.

This ticket SUPERSEDES T3 (shipped in #40, removed from this file by the same change). T3's raw-ANSI mandate ("DO NOT use blessed or any external dependencies") and its "Exactly zero dependencies" acceptance criterion are explicitly RETIRED and no longer apply to `lib/tui.mjs`.

The authoritative layout contract is NOT T3's prose (the as-built pane widths and column sizes deliberately diverge from it). It is the as-built `renderTuiState(state, width, height) -> string` in `lib/tui.mjs` at HEAD, whose visible output the six existing tests only SPOT-CHECK via substring assertions (`assert.ok(frame.includes(...))` at `test/tui.test.mjs:69-72, 94-97, 115`). Be aware they pin NOTHING about pane widths, column positions, padding, or the separators — "preserve its output exactly" has no pre-existing mechanical check. Therefore, BEFORE changing anything: generate a golden snapshot from HEAD's `renderTuiState` across several states and viewport sizes, and assert the rewrite reproduces it byte-for-byte. That golden, not the existing tests, is what actually protects the layout.

## Why (measured, not asserted)

`render()` is `process.stdout.write('\x1b[H' + renderTuiState(state, cols, rows))` on a 100ms `setInterval`, with no frame-committing layer. Measured against the real `renderTuiState` at 80x24:

- Idle, nothing changed: 212,600 bytes written per 10s, while 0 of 24 lines actually differ.
- Typical run (1 event/sec): 212,600 bytes per 10s; only 1 of 24 lines changes per tick. A line diff reduces this to 4,710 bytes (-97.8%).
- The cursor is never hidden (no `\x1b[?25l`), so a blinking cursor is dragged across all 24 rows 10x/sec.
- No synchronized output (DECSET 2026), so the emulator presents partial frames mid-write -> tearing.
- `padTruncate()` measures columns with `String.length`. A CJK grapheme counts as 1 column but occupies 2. A transcript containing Japanese text renders a 115-column line into an 80-column viewport: it wraps, pushes every following line down, and scrolls the buffer, so the whole frame jumps on each repaint. The same bug splits emoji surrogate pairs, emitting invalid UTF-8.
- `state.events` grows unbounded and every frame rebuilds strings from the entire history to display ~11 visible lines: 0.03ms/frame at 10 events, 12.21ms/frame at 20,000.

## Authorizations (these override T3)

1. ADD `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (`^0.80.10`) to `dependencies` in `package.json`. It brings 2 transitive deps: `get-east-asian-width`, `marked`.
2. BUMP `engines.node` in `package.json` from `>=18` to `>=22.19.0` to match pi-tui's floor, and DROP 18 and 20 from the `node-version` matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, leaving `[22]`. Both are past EOL (18: 2025-04-30, 20: 2026-04-30). Precision on the mechanism, because the naive version of this claim is wrong: there is no `.npmrc` in this repo, so `engine-strict` is OFF and npm treats an `engines` mismatch as an EBADENGINE *warning*, not an install failure — Node 18/20 CAN install pi-tui, they just cannot reliably RUN it. The transitive deps don't force 22 either (`get-east-asian-width@1.6.0` is `>=18`, `marked@18.0.5` is `>=20`). The matrix drop rests on pi-tui's own `>=22.19.0` floor and on those runners being past EOL, NOT on install failing. This is a BREAKING change for a published package (currently 0.4.3 on npm at `>=18`): release as 0.5.0 with a Breaking heading in `CHANGELOG.md`. Do not ship it as a patch.
2a. ALSO bump `.github/workflows/publish.yml` (line ~49) from `node-version: 20` to `22`. It is a separate workflow from ci.yml and it publishes the package; leaving it on Node 20 would publish a Node-22-only package from a runner that cannot install its own dependencies. TRAP — read the existing comment above `npm install -g npm@11` before touching it: that pin is deliberate. Node 20 ships npm 10.x, which cannot do OIDC trusted publishing, so npm >= 11.5.1 is required to mint a registry token from the GitHub id-token. KEEP the `npm@11` pin after the Node bump. Do NOT 'simplify' it to `npm@latest`: npm 12 requires node `^22.22 || ^24.15 || >=26`, and `engines` permits 22.19, so `npm@latest` can fail EBADENGINE on a conforming runner. npm 11 supports `^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0` and therefore spans both. Update that comment's now-stale 'Node 20 ships npm 10.x' wording to match reality.
2b. NOTE: `.github/workflows/**` is CODEOWNERS-protected (@voodootikigod) under branch protection with `enforce_admins: true`. Both workflow edits are in scope for this ticket, but merging still requires Code Owner review. Do not attempt to route around that.
3. DROP the alternate screen. pi-tui never emits `\x1b[?1049h` by design; it renders differentially into native scrollback. The dashboard no longer clears the screen on entry or exit, and its final frame remains in scrollback. Remove the `\x1b[?1049h`/`\x1b[?1049l` pair rather than trying to reintroduce it around pi-tui.

## Requirements

1. Preserve `launchTUI(repo, isWatch, intervalMs)`'s exported signature and its FULL exit-code contract. Two call sites: `bin/agb.mjs:235` (isWatch=true) and `bin/agb.mjs:314` (isWatch=false). Verified against HEAD: for a non-TTY, or a terminal narrower than 80 cols / shorter than 24 rows, `lib/tui.mjs:140`, `:150` and `:303` each return `isWatch ? 'fallback' : 0` — so `'fallback'` occurs ONLY when isWatch===true, and `bin/agb.mjs:315`'s `code === 'fallback' ? 0 : code` is dead on the `:314` path (benign: both spellings exit 0). Otherwise `0` (done, no failures), `2` (done, `report.failed` non-empty), `130` (ctrl-c), `1` (`q` pressed before done). Preserve this exactly, INCLUDING the isWatch asymmetry — do not 'tidy' it into an unconditional `'fallback'`.
2. `intervalMs` KEEPS its current meaning and its 100ms default: it is the cadence at which `run.json` and the JSONL logs are POLLED for new data, and `bin/agb.mjs:235` passes `--interval` into it (the `tui` call site at `:314` omits it and takes the 100ms default). It no longer drives repaints. Rendering is request-driven: after a poll changes state, request a render; if state is unchanged, request nothing.
3. Preserve the non-TTY and small-terminal fallback: `console.log(renderStatus(repo))` then return `isWatch ? 'fallback' : 0` — see Requirement 1; it is NOT `'fallback'` unconditionally. `lib/status.mjs` must not be modified to accommodate the rewrite — the fallback contract is frozen by convention for this ticket (it is deliberately NOT declared in `rails`, because T1 legitimately scopes `lib/status.mjs` and a rail here would block it, and because a non-empty rails array arms the `.adlc/tickets.json` trust root).
4. KEEP the transcript sanitization. The transcript pane renders UNTRUSTED `agy` agent output. `stripAnsi()` must be applied to every prompt/output line before it reaches any pi-tui component. Do not delegate sanitization to pi-tui: its components legitimately emit ANSI, so it cannot distinguish agb's own styling from an injection in agent output.
5. `stripAnsi`, `padTruncate` and `renderTuiState` all REMAIN exported with unchanged signatures, and ALL SIX existing tests in `test/tui.test.mjs` (blocks at lines 13, 31, 39, 47, 75, 100) must pass UNMODIFIED. This is a hard constraint, not a preference: weakening or rewriting an existing test to accommodate the rewrite is the failure mode this ticket most needs to avoid. Note that a width-correct `padTruncate` still satisfies every existing assertion — `padTruncate('very', 2) === 've'`, `padTruncate('very long string', 10) === 'very lo...'`, `padTruncate(null, 5) === '     '` — because those inputs are all single-column ASCII. Verify rather than assume. Add new tests; do not edit old ones.
6. Respect pi-tui's hard width invariant: it dumps `~/.pi/agent/pi-crash.log`, calls `stop()`, and THROWS if any rendered line exceeds viewport width (`dist/tui.js` ~:1230 and ~:1245). Fix `padTruncate` by swapping ONLY its `String.length` measurement for pi-tui's exported `visibleWidth()`, using `sliceByColumn()` (also exported) for grapheme-safe slicing. DO NOT substitute `truncateToWidth()` for `padTruncate` wholesale — it is NOT a drop-in and it BREAKS Requirement 5. Verified against 0.80.10: `truncateToWidth('very', 2)` returns `"\x1b[0m..\x1b[0m"` (not `'ve'`, breaking `test/tui.test.mjs:43`) and `truncateToWidth('very long string', 10)` returns `"very lo\x1b[0m...\x1b[0m"` (not `'very lo...'`, breaking `:42`), because it injects ANSI resets on every truncation — which also conflicts with Requirement 4's sanitization stance. Requirement 5 is the trump: keep `padTruncate`'s own ellipsis/slice logic at `lib/tui.mjs:17-20` and change only how columns are COUNTED. A reference implementation using `Intl.Segmenter` + `visibleWidth` has been verified to satisfy all five existing padTruncate assertions unmodified while rendering CJK at exactly the right column count and never emitting a lone surrogate.
7. Keep `renderTuiState` a pure `state -> string` function and adapt it to pi-tui's `Component { render(width): string[] }` contract with a thin wrapper that splits its output. Do not push layout into pi-tui components; that would break Requirement 5.
8. Cap `state.events` at a bounded ring buffer (2000 entries) so render cost is O(viewport), not O(run length).
9. Preserve keybindings: up/down select ticket, enter toggles transcript, `[`/`]` scroll timeline, home/end jump timeline, pageup/pagedown scroll transcript, `q` quit, ctrl-c -> 130.
10. Restore the cursor on every exit path, including crash and SIGINT/SIGTERM. A process that dies with the cursor hidden leaves the user's terminal permanently broken.

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm test` passes, and all six pre-existing `test/tui.test.mjs` tests pass with a zero-line diff against HEAD.
- `npm run coverage:check` still meets thresholds (lines 84, branches 75, functions 90).
- New regression test: a frame whose transcript contains CJK and emoji renders with EVERY line at or under the viewport width, measured in TERMINAL COLUMNS via `visibleWidth()`, not `String.length` (guards the 115-column bug).
- New test: two consecutive renders with unchanged state write ZERO bytes. Inject a fake `Terminal` (pi-tui exports the `Terminal` interface; `ProcessTerminal` is the real one) and assert on captured writes.
- New test: `padTruncate` never emits a lone surrogate for emoji input.
- Fallback path is exercised DIRECTLY, not via the CLI: call `launchTUI()` with a non-TTY stdout and assert it returns `0` for isWatch=false and `'fallback'` for isWatch=true. (Note `bin/agb.mjs:309-311` short-circuits the non-TTY case BEFORE `lib/tui.mjs` is imported, so piping `agb tui` to a file is a vacuous check — it passes regardless of the rewrite and never reaches Requirement 3's code.)
- `agb status --watch --ui` still resolves 2 when `report.failed` is non-empty.
- `adlc hollow-test --test-cmd "npm test" --base main` surfaces no new survivors in `lib/tui.mjs`.

tickets.title: [P3] fix: strikes column always renders blank
tickets.body:
The Strikes column in the `agb tui` ticket table is always blank. Root cause: `renderTuiState` calls `padTruncate(strikesVal, 10, 'right')` with a number (or an array), and `padTruncate`'s first line is `str = stripAnsi(str)`, which returns '' for any non-string input. So every numeric strike count renders as 10 spaces.

This is PRE-EXISTING (it predates the pi-tui rebuild in T-TUI-RENDER and was preserved byte-for-byte by that behavior-preserving refactor). It was surfaced by `adlc hollow-test`: the mutants `t.strikes ?? 0 -> ?? 1` and negating `if (Array.isArray(strikesVal))` both survive precisely because their outputs are flattened to '' by stripAnsi, so no test can distinguish them.

Fix: coerce the strike count to a string before it reaches padTruncate (e.g. `String(strikesVal)` at the call site), or handle numbers in padTruncate. Whichever is chosen, do NOT weaken stripAnsi's non-string guard — it is a security boundary for untrusted transcript text.

Acceptance criteria:
- A ticket with `strikes: 3` renders `3` in the Strikes column; `strikes: [1,2]` renders `2` (the array length, per the existing `Array.isArray` branch).
- A ticket with no `strikes` field renders `0`.
- The two named hollow-test mutants are now killed.
- Regenerate `test/fixtures/tui-golden.json` (the golden layout fixture) since strike cells change from blank to a number, and confirm the diff is limited to strike columns.
- `npm test` and `npm run coverage:check` pass.
